bug_semantics: Repo.init accepted arbitrary keyword options and forwarded them to git init without applying GitPython's unsafe-option policy. An attacker who can control template=<directory> can make git init copy executable hooks from that directory into the new repository; a later Git operation such as commit executes the planted hook with the application's privileges. The same unguarded sink also accepted separate_git_dir redirection.
flaw_origin: Commit 00c5497f190172765cc7a53ff9d8852a26b91676 generalized the predecessor's bare-only initializer into the public Repo.init API, removed the mandatory --bare argument, retained unrestricted **kwargs, and called git.init(path, **kwargs). Its test explicitly exercised Repo.init(..., template=...). This was not merely a name-only move: enabling ordinary non-bare initialization created the reported template-hook-to-next-commit execution path. A later correction, 15ee0ac0d56a5fb5ba13fae4288621ddd2185f17, changed the call to git.init(**kwargs) but preserved the unsafe option flow, so it is not the introducer.

Commit-minimality reconciliation 2026-08-29: introducer corrected to 33ebe7acec14b25c5f84f35a664803fcab2f7781 after first-write/ancestry re-verification (see evidence tail). introducer_parent corrected to null (root commit) (same recheck). BIC correction 2026-08-29: introducer_sha 00c5497f190172765cc7a53ff9d8852a26b91676 -> 33ebe7acec14b25c5f84f35a664803fcab2f7781 after line-level first-write re-verification (see evidence tail). The vulnerability is an unsafe option-forwarding design error, not shell-string interpolation: GitPython converts the caller's template keyword into a real git-init option, and Git itself performs the dangerous hook copy. The smallest causal change for the advisory's Repo.init attack path is 00c5497f190172765cc7a53ff9d8852a26b91676. Although that commit starts from an init_bare predecessor, it materially removes forced bare initialization and exposes general Repo.init while deliberately preserving arbitrary option forwarding; its own test proves template passed through that new entry point. The immediate parent contains only the bare-specific predecessor, so the reported ordinary repository followed by commit-hook execution path is absent there. Later edits merely correct or restyle the same flow. The BIC is a normal single-parent semantic commit, not a merge, squash, revert, or reconstructed aggregate. The flaw remains through 3.1.57. Direct fix d9ddb55bdc66ffe8c9932fe460e6b8c8211e47c7 applies the missing denylist before filesystem mutation and is contained by the first patched tag 3.1.58. Finally, the exact BIC commit object has human author/committer identities and no AI attribution marker, so the causal verdict is NOT_AI; attribution signals outside that BIC are not used.
